findings.description: The cloud pedagogy guard constructor sets can_solve false but retains a categorical step and answer. Four train guards (missing_side, inconsistent_counts, missing_image, zero_groups) use it. The primary authoring validator forbids any steps/answers when can_solve is false. This is not a fabricated numeric answer: it is an inconsistent neutral refusal convention that should be made explicit before further export.
findings.recommended_action: Root inspect selected actual train guards and choose one declared neutral refusal convention; retain original source hashes and derive corrected views only if needed.

findings.description: H(a,b,c) assigns the same three questions to many authored topics. The task-specific hint statement may be useful, so the shared question alone is not always a failure. However level-2 guidance can refer to an unspecified relationship if its statement does not name the operation. The parser checks presence/order/question marks, not relevance or increasing specificity.
findings.recommended_action: Inspect selected full hint+question pairs; require a specific operation/relationship and a feasible next action rather than globally replacing every shared question.

findings.description: Arithmetic checks bind machine-readable expression/result fields; they do not establish correctness of arbitrary numerical prose or its agreement with the requested quantity. A synthetic audit-only row with correct 453-128=325 expression/result but false explanation 13−8=4 passes inspect_case. This is a validator counterexample, not a claim that this false explanation exists in training. In multidigit validation, embedded-expression processing checks evaluability and signature coverage, but not the textual equality RHS; subtraction carry metadata checks do not independently verify every prose token.
findings.recommended_action: Root read actual numeric prose in selected rows; any derived repair should check all prose equalities and intermediate quantities alongside expression/result, with source-hash lineage.

findings.description: Worked targets intentionally use can_solve, initial_guidance, steps and answer; hint targets use hint/question. The saved contract explicitly separates this from live PlanDraft canSolve/topic/goal/steps/finalAnswerStep and requires a reviewed adapter. JSON format alone is not a semantic error. Numeric machine-readable and prose values must still agree. Neutral hints map levels1..3 to runtime0..2 only after stage/no-number/pedagogy checks.
findings.recommended_action: Keep the bounded retrain task in a documented neutral tutor contract; do not claim runtime API compatibility or add live schema fields to data without the explicit conversion boundary.

findings.description: Current exhaustive subtraction correctly updates the donor, intervening zeros and current column. Current fraction recipes use LCM/cross-products/Fraction with nonzero-divisor guards. The finite grade2 453−128 and427−156 authored explanations also update the correct donor column. No wrong numerical target was reproduced from these current helpers in the declared bounded checks. Decimal generator inputs are k/10 and its claim that both inputs have one decimal place is valid only inside that narrow representation domain, not a rule for arbitrary decimal word problems.
findings.recommended_action: Do not invent a generator bug from model errors or regenerate the corpus. Compare current source hashes with the actual selected target rows; repair concrete observed bad targets separately from model learning failures.

bounded_cpu_checks.execution_method: AST extract named pure functions only; no module main/import side effects, protection functions, corpus files, or app runtime invoked. Fraction signature helper replaced with a SHA256 stub because signature implementation is outside numeric target checking.
